items.title: How a Self-Described ‘Junkie’ Rode Synthetic Drugs to Oblivion — and Fame
items.summary: An Estonian addict could barely keep pace with the new drugs flooding the market. His terrifying accounts of the cruel toll they took on his body held his country in its grip.

items.title: Trump and His Aides Helped Bolsonaro Flee Brazil and Enter U.S.
items.summary: President Trump ensured Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost a presidential election in Brazil and faces multiple criminal investigations there, could enter the United States, U.S. officials said.

items.title: With No Clear Winner, How Could Israel Get a Prime Minister?
items.summary: Deadlock is possible, as neither the bloc of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his main challenger appear likely to win a majority. But there are still paths to a new government.

items.title: U.S. Hits Rwanda With New Sanctions Over a Conflict Trump Declared ‘Ended’
items.summary: The Treasury Department accused Rwanda of undermining a U.S.-brokered peace agreement by supporting a rebel group in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

items.title: Suspect in France Shootings Said He Targeted Muslims and Africans, Prosecutor Says
items.summary: The suspect, identified only as Kévin T., admitted to planning the attacks near Paris last week, the prosecutor said. One person was killed and seven wounded.

items.title: Haiti Postpones Elections as Gang Violence Runs Rampant
items.summary: Haiti is in the throes of debilitating gang violence, which has kept officials from organizing an election to pick a new president.

items.title: China Is Not Happy About Fan-made A.I. Videos of Sun Wukong and Lin Daiyu
items.summary: Mash-up videos of beloved characters from Chinese classics — some made with A.I. — have caught the attention of the authorities.

items.title: In Marseille, Macron Confronts a Potent Mix of France’s Problems
items.summary: France’s second city, five years into a presidential development plan, is grappling with the social strains that have fueled protests across the country.

items.title: After Crash, Spain Asks if Its Train System Is Too Old and Prone to Human Error
items.summary: After the country’s second major rail disaster in a year, Spaniards were confronting questions about the safety of their once-vaunted rail system.

items.title: China Confirms Expulsion of 33 Officials, as Xi’s Purge Deepens
items.summary: Xi Jinping has enforced loyalty as he prepares to claim a fourth term as leader. Among those removed was a prominent former diplomat, Liu Jianchao.

items.title: Polymarket Is Investigating Suspicious Bets on Israeli Election
items.summary: The company said it was looking into hundreds of new accounts that had placed wagers in two markets related to the election on Tuesday.

items.title: Big Tech’s Data Center Blitz Is Burning Through Cash and Scaring Wall St.
items.summary: Amazon on Thursday became the latest tech company to announce swelling investments in A.I. amid stumbling share prices.

items.title: Inflation Accelerated in October, PCE Index Shows
items.summary: The Personal Consumption Expenditures index picked up in September, according to data released a day after the Federal Reserve’s decision to hold interest rates steady.

items.title: U.S. GDP Increased 3.4% in Third Quarter
items.summary: The economy grew 3.4 percent in the third quarter, the fastest pace in a year. Strong spending and growth contrast with the poor marks many voters are giving the economy.

items.title: Microsoft Up, Google Down. A Tale of Two Hyperscalers.
items.summary: Investors are showing little patience for lavish spending and meager returns on companies’ artificial intelligence bets.

items.title: Its Investors Say Kalshi Is Worth $40 Billion. Is an I.P.O. Next?
items.summary: The prediction market raised $1 billion in a new funding round and landed a market value almost double that of rival Polymarket. But legal challenges to its business persist.

items.title: Volkswagen ‘Must Act Quickly’ After Largest Loss in Over a Decade
items.summary: The German carmaker warned that it “must act quickly and decisively” to cut costs.

items.title: DoorDash to Buy Instacart for $17 Billion, Uniting 2 Delivery Giants
items.summary: The deal combines the country’s largest restaurant delivery service with its biggest online grocery platform.

items.title: Hong Kong Leader Apologizes for Deadly Apartment Building Fire
items.summary: John Lee, the city’s chief executive, said his housing secretary would step down, but he vehemently defended the government.

items.title: Christine Lagarde to Step Down as President of European Central Bank
items.summary: Her plan to depart in February, months before the end of an eight-year term, sets in motion a selection process among European leaders for a new central bank president.

items.title: Intel’s Shares Plunge 20% as A.I. Hinders Some Parts of Its Business
items.summary: The chipmaker, whose largest investor is the U.S. government, reported that the A.I. boom’s domino effect had hurt sales to personal computer makers.

items.title: Polymarket and Kalshi Turn Midterm Elections Into a Multimillion Dollar Market
items.summary: Betting markets like Polymarket and Kalshi have transformed America’s democracy into a new kind of casino.

items.title: Nvidia Chief, Jensen Huang, Is Seen as Target of Chinese Spy Plot
items.summary: A Chinese businesswoman who had a close relationship with Jensen Huang was found to be passing intelligence to Beijing. President Trump was briefed and took no action.

items.title: Hit the Road This Season With These Useful New Map Features
items.summary: The recent updates to Google Maps and Apple’s Maps use artificial (and human) intelligence for better navigation, planning and travel guides.

items.title: Bodacious A.I. Bots Are Stealing Jokes From Young Female Comedians
items.summary: Swiping jokes word for word, these bodacious bots mainly lift from young female comedians. What’s so insidious is how they’re subtly changing us, the audience.

items.title: Alphabet’s Revenue Rises 25% as Profit Falls
items.summary: The company has been spending relentlessly to build A.I. and said it would increase those investments next year. Profit dropped because of changes to the value of its investments.

items.title: Microsoft’s Profit Jumps 32% Despite Big Increase in Spending
items.summary: The company’s free cash flow stayed positive in the last quarter even as it spent $45.2 billion on capital expenses like data centers and offered to pay workers to leave.

items.title: Apple Unveils Its First Touch-Screen MacBook Pro
items.summary: Steve Jobs and Tim Cook both dismissed the idea, but Apple’s new chief executive is reimagining some of the company’s most important products.
